note: Feeds the daily news digest reads (scripts/fetch-news.ts). RSS or Atom only: a site without a feed is not scraped. Every entry was fetched and parsed on 2026-09-07, and each one twice, by whoever added it and by a second pass that checked what the items are actually about. cnadnr.ro, mt.ro, cnir.ro, metrorex.ro, gov.ro and Bulgaria's api.bg time out from outside their own country, though cfr.ro does not, so a Romanian state host is not automatically unreachable. cnair.ro is not CNAIR but a squatted domain serving a single 2016 post. clubferoviar.ro and proinfrastructura.ro were dropped: both now answer any non-browser client with a JavaScript challenge, on every feed path tried. srbijavoz.rs was dropped because its pubDate values are transliterated into Cyrillic and no parser reads them. The EIB project pipeline was dropped because the host's robots.txt asks clients not to fetch feeds. koridorisrbije.rs is an empty Angular shell, so the corridors are covered through mgsi and putevi-srbije instead. A general feed is filtered to items that name a section or use infrastructure vocabulary; a trade feed is kept whole, which is why an international title is filed as general. Wikipedia article histories are watched from the projects' own sources and need no entry here. The three Greek entries were fetched and parsed with the digest's own client on 2026-09-28. ergose.gr has a working feed but was left out: its newest item was from January 2025. The Croatian feeds were fetched and parsed with the digest's own client on 2026-10-05. hzinfra.hr (HŽ Infrastruktura, https://www.hzinfra.hr/feed/) was left out: the feed is live and parses, but the host serves an incomplete certificate chain (no intermediate), so Node's default fetch fails with UNABLE_TO_VERIFY_LEAF_SIGNATURE and only succeeds with --use-system-ca; the digest would error on it every day. Recheck if the host fixes its chain. n1info.hr and tportal.hr parse but are whole-newsroom feeds with almost nothing on infrastructure in the sample, and one general Croatian feed is enough. The two Czech entries were fetched and parsed with the digest's own client on 2026-10-05. nku.cz/cz/rss.xml and sfdi.gov.cz/feed/ also parse (30 and 10 items) but were left out: the audit office feed is mostly accounting audits, vacancies and meeting notices with a transport audit only occasionally, and the SFDI feed carries funding rules and contract amendments, ten items spanning April to September 2026.

sources.name: Economedia
sources.note: Business daily with a regular infrastructure beat.

sources.name: Profit.ro
sources.note: Served with a text/html content type; the body is RSS 2.0.

sources.name: CFR SA
sources.note: The national rail infrastructure manager. Line closures, restorations and works notices, same day.

sources.name: Ministarstvo građevinarstva, saobraćaja i infrastrukture
sources.note: The Serbian construction and transport ministry. Cyrillic, which the matcher transliterates before scoring.

sources.name: JP Putevi Srbije
sources.note: The roads authority. A Joomla category feed, which is why the site looked feedless: the plain URL serves HTML.

sources.name: Infrastruktura železnice Srbije
sources.note: The rail infrastructure manager. Carries tender notices for the Belgrade to Niš high speed line.

sources.name: Metropolitan Sofia
sources.note: Sofia Metro, the operator that opens the stations. The feed is linked from the homepage; the catalogue previously recorded this host as a 404, which was simply wrong.

sources.name: Ypodomes.com
sources.note: Greek infrastructure trade site. Greek script, which the matcher romanises before scoring. The feed carries only its latest ten items, all from the same day when checked, so a digest that skips a day misses some.

sources.name: Egnatia Odos S.A.
sources.note: The Egnatia Odos motorway company. Low volume, mostly tenders and works notices: ten items spanning September 2025 to August 2026 when checked.

sources.name: eKathimerini
sources.note: English edition of Kathimerini. Filed as general: the feed is the whole paper, forty items a day.

sources.name: Poslovni dnevnik
sources.note: Croatian business daily. Filed as general: twenty items a day from the whole paper, of which a few concern roads and rail (a new deadline for an expressway section to Koprivnica among the twenty checked).

sources.name: CINEA
sources.note: The agency that awards Connecting Europe Facility money, where a cross border project is named before it is built. Filed as general: 20 of its 30 current items are the LIFE environment programme and none names these three countries, so it earns its place on the rare transport award rather than on volume.

sources.name: European Commission, Mobility and Transport
sources.note: Corridor policy and funding decisions. Filed as general: mostly aviation, maritime and passenger rights, with about five items in thirty touching road or rail.

sources.name: Railway PRO
sources.note: Published in Romania, written in English, covers all three countries. Filed as general: one of its thirty current items names any of them, so the vocabulary filter earns its keep here.

sources.name: Railway Gazette International
sources.note: International rail trade press. Filed as general for the same reason: none of its twelve current items concerns these three countries. Its terms permit reference use and forbid training.

sources.name: Zdopravy.cz
sources.note: Czech transport trade press covering roads, rail, trams and the Prague and Brno networks. Hundred items spanning about three days when checked, so a digest that skips a few days misses some. It also carries aviation and vehicle-industry items, which match no project.

sources.name: České dálnice
sources.note: Czech motorway news site. Low volume, mostly openings and construction starts reported from ŘSD: ten items spanning December 2025 to October 2026 when checked.
